title: Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry analysis for identification and quantification of antimicrobial compounds in distillery wastewater
author: Hou, Ling, et al.

steps.title: Prepare stock and working solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve each standard analyte in 50 % methanol to obtain a concentrated stock solution at 1 mg mL⁻¹. Dilute the stock with acetonitrile to generate a series of working solutions that will be used to build the calibration curve. Store all solutions at –20 °C until use.

substeps.instruction: Weigh the appropriate amount of each standard and dissolve in 50 % methanol to a concentration of 1 mg mL⁻¹ (stock solution).
Dilute the stock solution with acetonitrile to produce the required calibration working solutions.
Label and keep all prepared solutions at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare wastewater sample
steps.instruction: Treat the distillery wastewater by dilution and centrifugation before LC‑MS/MS injection.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µL of the wastewater sample to 20 mL of 50 % methanol.
Vortex the mixture for 2 min.
Centrifuge at 13 000 rpm for 10 min at 4 °C.
Transfer the supernatant to a new tube.
Centrifuge the transferred supernatant again at 13 000 rpm for 5 min at 4 °C.
Inject the final supernatant into the HPLC‑MS/MS system for analysis.

steps.title: Construct calibration curve
steps.instruction: Generate five concentration levels for each analyte, acquire LC‑MS/MS data, and perform weighted linear regression to obtain calibration equations, linear ranges, R² values and the instrumental detection limit.

substeps.instruction: Prepare five calibration standards for each analyte covering the following linear ranges:
• Lactic acid: 375–75 000 ng mL⁻¹ (R² = 0.9985), equation Y = 61.991 + 3.7752·X
• Succinic acid: 50–10 000 ng mL⁻¹ (R² = 0.9902), equation Y = ‑1108.29 + 65.2021·X
• Acetophenone: 50–10 000 ng mL⁻¹ (R² = 0.9983), equation Y = 296.551 + 61.5398·X
• Cinnamic acid: 50–10 000 ng mL⁻¹ (R² = 0.9991), equation Y = 73.5861 + 15.9079·X
• Phenyllactic acid: 50–10 000 ng mL⁻¹ (R² = 0.9984), equation Y = 2286.28 + 1166.98·X
Run each standard on the HPLC‑MS/MS under the same conditions as the samples.
Perform linear regression of peak area (Y) versus concentration (X) weighted by 1⁄X².
Determine the instrumental detection limit (IDL) as the concentration giving a signal‑to‑noise ratio of 3.
Confirm that all R² values are ≥ 0.9981.

steps.title: Validate method with spiked samples
steps.instruction: Assess precision and extraction recovery by analyzing wastewater spiked at three concentration levels of the target organic acids.

substeps.instruction: Prepare low, medium, and high concentration spike solutions of the five analytes.
Add each spike level to separate aliquots of wastewater, creating five replicates per level (total 15 validation samples).
Process the spiked samples using the same preparation procedure described in Step 2.
Analyze the samples by LC‑MS/MS and calculate:
– Recovery (relative error, RE) for each analyte (expected 95.89 %–116.39 %).
– Precision as relative standard deviation (RSD) (expected < 9.80 %).
Verify that recoveries meet acceptance criteria and that matrix effects are negligible.
